article.title: Why the Best Prediction Threshold Is a Business Decision, Not a Model Property
article.why: Practical analytical English for customer and model decision making.

paragraphs.en:
The common 0.5 classification threshold is a convention, not a universal business rule. The correct operating point depends on what action follows the score.

Capacity can determine the cutoff directly. If a team can contact only one hundred thousand customers, the practical threshold may be the score of the one-hundred-thousandth ranked customer.

Economics also matters. Contact cost, expected margin, false-positive cost, customer fatigue, and channel expense can make a lower or higher threshold appropriate.

Calibration is necessary when a score is interpreted as a probability. Good ranking does not guarantee that a score of 0.20 corresponds to a twenty-percent event rate.

Propensity is also different from incremental treatment effect. A high-propensity customer may purchase without contact, so uplift or causal estimates can be more relevant for campaign decisions.

Teams should compare candidate cutoffs using precision, recall, lift, expected profit, incremental conversions, and capacity utilization. The chosen threshold should be documented with its assumptions.

Thresholds should be versioned separately from models because capacity, margin, costs, or policy can change while the predictive model remains unchanged.

The model produces information; the business chooses an action. Threshold design is the decision layer connecting those two functions.

Analysts should state the comparison population and time period clearly so that a numerical change is not confused with a change in customer composition.

Business interpretation improves when absolute values, relative rates, and operational constraints are reviewed together rather than as isolated model metrics.

A robust decision rule should remain understandable to the people who operate it, because implementation details can change the value of an otherwise strong analytical result.
